subject: Biology
description: Transpiration, stomata, xylem-phloem transport, plant hormones (auxin, gibberellin, ABA, ethylene)

questions.stem: TRANSPIRATION in plants is the process of:

options.option_text: Absorption of water from the soil through plant root hairs
Loss of water vapour from leaves, mostly through stomata
Conversion of sunlight energy into chemical energy in chloroplasts
Movement of sugar from leaves to other parts of the plant

questions.explanation: Transpiration — water vapour loss from aerial parts of plants, mostly via STOMATA on leaves (also some via cuticle, lenticels). Drives the 'transpiration pull' that lifts water through the xylem from roots to leaves — the cohesion-tension mechanism of long-distance transport. ~99% of water absorbed is transpired; only ~1% used in photosynthesis. Distractor 1 = absorption / root pressure. Distractor 3 = photosynthesis. Distractor 4 = translocation (sugar movement via phloem).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: STOMATA on leaves are openings flanked by which specialised cells?

options.option_text: Sieve elements that move sugars within the plant
Guard cells, which open and close the stomatal pore
Tracheids that conduct water within the plant
Companion cells in the phloem of the plant

questions.explanation: Stoma (singular; pl. stomata) — pore in the leaf epidermis. Flanked by two GUARD CELLS — kidney-shaped (in dicots) or dumbbell-shaped (grasses). When turgid (water-filled) → curve outward → stoma opens for gas exchange. When flaccid → close. Open during day (CO₂ in for photosynthesis); close at night to limit water loss. CAM plants (cacti, pineapple) reverse this — open stomata at night. Distractors 1, 3, 4 are vascular-tissue cells, not at the leaf surface.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: XYLEM tissue in plants is responsible primarily for:

options.option_text: Transport of organic food from leaves to roots
Upward transport of water and minerals from roots
Storage of starch grains within the plant body
Anchoring the plant firmly into the soil

questions.explanation: XYLEM — water + minerals from roots upward to leaves. UNIDIRECTIONAL flow. Cells: tracheids + vessel elements (DEAD at maturity, hollow tubes). Driven by transpiration pull + root pressure. PHLOEM — sugar (sucrose) translocation, BIDIRECTIONAL — leaves to growing parts / storage organs. Cells: sieve tube elements + companion cells (alive at maturity). Distractor 1 = phloem function. Distractor 3 = parenchyma role. Distractor 4 = root system mechanical role.

questions.stem: AUXIN, the plant hormone discovered by Charles Darwin's experiments on phototropism, is now known to be:

options.option_text: Cytokinin, found in the coconut milk used in tissue culture
Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), produced at the shoot tip
Abscisic acid (ABA), a stress hormone in seeds
Ethylene, the gas that ripens stored fruits

questions.explanation: Auxin — first identified plant hormone (Darwin, 1880; isolated as IAA by Went, 1928). Made at SHOOT APEX, transports basipetally (downward), promotes cell elongation. Causes phototropism (more auxin on shaded side → that side elongates → bend toward light). Used commercially: 2,4-D (synthetic auxin) as selective herbicide for broadleaf weeds; root-promoting hormone (IBA) in propagation. Distractor 1 = cytokinin (cell division). Distractor 3 = ABA (stress / dormancy). Distractor 4 = ethylene (fruit ripening, leaf abscission).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: ETHYLENE is the only plant hormone that is a GAS at room temperature. It is responsible primarily for:

options.option_text: Promoting elongation of plant stems and shoots
Ripening of climacteric fruits like banana and mango
Inducing seed dormancy in autumn cold conditions
Cell division and lateral bud growth in the stem

questions.explanation: Ethylene (C₂H₄) — gaseous hormone. Triggers fruit ripening (climacteric fruits — mango, banana, apple, papaya, tomato — show a respiratory peak associated with ethylene release). Also leaf + flower senescence (yellowing, dropping), abscission. EXPLOITED commercially: ethephon (chemical that releases ethylene) used to ripen mangoes / bananas after transport — but illegal CALCIUM CARBIDE ripening (which produces acetylene + arsenic/phosphorus traces) is a serious health concern in India and is banned. Distractor 1 = auxin / gibberellin. Distractor 3 = ABA. Distractor 4 = cytokinin.

questions.stem: GIBBERELLINS are plant hormones discovered originally from a:

options.option_text: Bacterium found in human gut microbiome
Fungus that infected rice plants in Japan
Virus attacking tomato plants in Europe
Root nodule of leguminous plants in tropics

questions.explanation: Gibberellins — first noted in 1926 by Japanese botanist Eiichi Kurosawa studying 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease in rice — caused by the fungus GIBBERELLA FUJIKUROI which made rice plants grow abnormally tall. The fungus secreted GIBBERELLINS — promote stem elongation, seed germination, flowering, fruit growth (e.g., elongates seedless grapes commercially). Now ~136 known forms (GA₁, GA₂, ...). Distractor 1, 3, 4 are unrelated.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: ABSCISIC ACID (ABA) is sometimes called the 'STRESS HORMONE' in plants because it:

options.option_text: Promotes flowering during drought conditions in arid regions
Closes stomata to reduce water loss under drought stress
Triggers seed germination in temperatures below freezing
Causes leaves to expand rapidly during winter dormancy

questions.explanation: ABA — produced in roots + leaves under DROUGHT or other stresses. Major actions: (1) closes stomata (signals guard cells) → reduces water loss; (2) induces seed dormancy (prevents germination during unfavourable conditions); (3) leaf abscission. Antagonistic to gibberellins (GA promotes germination, ABA inhibits — balance determines whether seed sprouts). Distractor 1 — opposite (ABA generally inhibits flowering). Distractor 3 — opposite of seed-germination effect. Distractor 4 — ABA induces dormancy, not expansion.
